name: SecOps-NG: EU AI Act Article 14 human-oversight operating loop

nodes.name: ai_human_oversight_start

values.name: __deployment_id__
values.description: Stable operator-side identifier of the high-risk AI system deployment this oversight cycle covers. Shared with playbook.eu_ai_act_deployer_obligations@v1 so the assignment record and this loop join on one key.

values.name: __oversight_cycle__
values.description: The review window this cycle runs against, as an RFC 3339 interval of two Zulu instants (<start>/<end>). Supplied by the operator's oversight cadence; every step reads it as it is.

values.name: __roster_entries__
values.description: The watch for the window, each exactly person_ref, natural_person, on_watch and reachable (real booleans), powers (the delegated Art. 14(4)(d)-(e) powers) and authority_ref (the delegation record, or null). CACAO v2 has no list type, so the value rides as a string carrying a JSON-native list; the compile target's adapter seam marshals it.

values.name: __roster_resolved_at__
values.description: Zulu instant (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) the roster is resolved at.

values.name: __instructions_ref__
values.description: Reference of the current version of the provider's Art. 13 instructions for use; a briefing against any other version does not count.

values.name: __briefings__
values.description: Briefing records, each exactly person_ref, deployment_id, instructions_ref, briefed_at (Zulu) and one real boolean per Art. 14(4)(a)-(c) limb: capacities_and_limitations, automation_bias_awareness and output_interpretation. CACAO v2 has no list type, so the value rides as a string carrying a JSON-native list; the compile target's adapter seam marshals it.

values.name: __briefing_recorded_at__
values.description: Zulu instant (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) the briefing record is composed at.

values.name: __flagged_decisions__
values.description: The outputs and decisions flagged for oversight in the window, each exactly decision_ref, flagged_at (Zulu, inside the window) and output_ref. CACAO v2 has no list type, so the value rides as a string carrying a JSON-native list; the compile target's adapter seam marshals it.

values.name: __reviews__
values.description: At most one review per flagged decision, each exactly decision_ref, reviewer_ref, reviewed_at (Zulu) and disposition (upheld or intervened). CACAO v2 has no list type, so the value rides as a string carrying a JSON-native list; the compile target's adapter seam marshals it.

values.name: __biometric_record__
values.description: Exactly annex_iii_point_1a (a real boolean), exemption_legal_basis_ref (the Union or national law relied on for the Art. 14(5) exemption, or null) and verifications (each exactly decision_ref and verifier_refs).

values.name: __reviewed_at__
values.description: Zulu instant (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) the review pass closes.

values.name: __interventions__
values.description: One per decision dispositioned intervened, each exactly decision_ref, intervention_type, intervened_by (its reviewer), basis (text) and intervened_at (Zulu). An empty list closes the window with a nil record. CACAO v2 has no list type, so the value rides as a string carrying a JSON-native list; the compile target's adapter seam marshals it.

values.name: __intervention_recorded_at__
values.description: Zulu instant (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) the intervention record is composed at.

values.name: __workflow_id__
values.description: Identifier of the workflow, folded into the evidence artifact_id.

values.name: __execution_id__
values.description: Identifier of this execution, folded into the evidence artifact_id.

values.name: __captured_at__
values.description: Zulu instant (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) the evidence is captured at, folded into its artifact_id.

values.name: __oversight_roster_id__
values.description: Identifier of the roster resolved for the window. Extracted at the compile target's adapter seam from __oversight_roster__.roster_id.

values.name: __briefing_record_id__
values.description: Identifier of the Art. 14(4)(a)-(c) briefing record. Extracted at the compile target's adapter seam from __briefing_record__.briefing_id.

values.name: __review_disposition_id__
values.description: Identifier of the window's review record, emitted even when the review found nothing. Extracted at the compile target's adapter seam from __review_disposition__.disposition_id.

values.name: __biometric_two_person_verification__
values.description: The Art. 14(5) record, present only for an Annex III point 1(a) remote biometric identification system and null otherwise: the decisions verified by two separate qualified natural persons, those that were not and so permit no action, or the legal basis of the exemption relied on. Extracted at the compile target's adapter seam from __review_disposition__.biometric_two_person_verification.

values.name: __intervention_record_id__
values.description: Identifier of the intervention record, or of the dated nil record when the window produced none. Extracted at the compile target's adapter seam from __intervention_record__.intervention_record_id.

values.name: __intervention_type__
values.description: Which Art. 14(4)(d)-(e) exercise occurred: none, decline_use, disregard_output, override_or_reverse_output, interrupt_operation, or multiple. Kept separate from the record because the exercises carry different weight on later review. Extracted at the compile target's adapter seam from __intervention_record__.intervention_type.

values.name: __oversight_evidence_id__
values.description: Identifier of the dated cycle-evidence artifact. Extracted at the compile target's adapter seam from __oversight_evidence__.artifact_id.

values.name: __oversight_roster__
values.description: Envelope the roster step emits: each entry with its powers and missing powers, the empowered and reachable overseers, and whether the roster is effective.

values.name: __briefing_record__
values.description: Envelope the briefing step emits: each empowered overseer's briefing and missing limbs, the rejected briefings with their reason, and whether everyone is briefed.

values.name: __review_disposition__
values.description: Envelope the review step emits: every flagged decision's disposition, the reviewed and intervened counts, the reviews that did not count, and the Art. 14(5) record.

values.name: __intervention_record__
values.description: Envelope the intervention step emits: each exercise with its type, basis, latency and the system output, the monitoring signals, or the nil record.

values.name: __oversight_evidence__
values.description: Envelope the evidence step emits: the four joined records and whether oversight was exercised, not merely assigned.

nodes.notes: Entry point. Fires on the operator's oversight cadence for a deployment already in service, and on the assignment edge handed over by the Art. 26(2) step of the deployer-obligations playbook.

nodes.name: establish_oversight_roster

parameters.pythonCode:
from content.playbooks.ai_human_oversight.primitives.roster import resolve_oversight_roster
__oversight_roster__ = resolve_oversight_roster(deployment_id=__deployment_id__, oversight_cycle=__oversight_cycle__, entries=__roster_entries__, resolved_at=__roster_resolved_at__)

nodes.notes: Resolve who holds human oversight of __deployment_id__ for __oversight_cycle__ and with what authority, and record the roster. Art. 26(2) makes the assignment; this step makes it operational for the window: who is on watch, what each is empowered to do, and who is reachable. The authority limb matters most: Art. 14(4)(d) and (e) require the overseer to be able to decline to use the system, disregard, override or reverse its output, and intervene in or interrupt its operation, so an entry counts as empowered only as a natural person with a delegation record and all four powers, and the roster is effective only when one such person on watch is reachable. Produces __oversight_roster__, from which __oversight_roster_id__ is extracted.

nodes.name: brief_oversight_personnel

parameters.pythonCode:
from content.playbooks.ai_human_oversight.primitives.briefing import compose_briefing_record
__briefing_record__ = compose_briefing_record(roster=__oversight_roster__, instructions_ref=__instructions_ref__, briefings=__briefings__, recorded_at=__briefing_recorded_at__)

nodes.notes: Check that every empowered overseer holds a current briefing against the provider's Art. 13 instructions for use, discharging the competence limbs of Art. 14(4): understanding the system's capacities and limitations well enough to detect anomalies (14(4)(a)), awareness of automation bias (14(4)(b)), and correct interpretation of the output (14(4)(c)). The briefing is per system and per instructions: one recorded for another deployment or a superseded version does not count, and is kept on the record as rejected. Produces __briefing_record__, from which __briefing_record_id__ is extracted.

nodes.name: review_flagged_decisions

parameters.pythonCode:
from content.playbooks.ai_human_oversight.primitives.review import review_flagged_decisions
__review_disposition__ = review_flagged_decisions(roster=__oversight_roster__, briefing=__briefing_record__, oversight_cycle=__oversight_cycle__, flagged=__flagged_decisions__, reviews=__reviews__, biometric=__biometric_record__, reviewed_at=__reviewed_at__)

nodes.notes: Run the standing review pass over the outputs and decisions flagged for oversight in __oversight_cycle__, and record the disposition of each: upheld, intervened, or unreviewed. Only an empowered, briefed overseer's review counts. A review that found nothing is as much evidence of oversight as an intervention. Carries the Art. 14(5) branch: for an Annex III point 1(a) remote biometric identification system, no action may be taken on an identification unless two separate qualified natural persons verified it, so an upheld identification without two permits no action, and one person confirming twice does not count. Where the law-enforcement, migration, border-control or asylum exemption is relied on, the record names the law relied on. Produces __review_disposition__, from which __review_disposition_id__ and __biometric_two_person_verification__ are extracted.

nodes.name: record_intervention
nodes.notes: Record each exercise of Art. 14(4)(d) or (e) the review produced, naming which of the four occurred: declining to use the system, disregarding its output, overriding or reversing it, or interrupting its operation. Each record captures who intervened, on what basis, the latency from the flag, and what the system had produced, because an intervention is also a signal the Art. 26(5) monitoring duty and the provider's Art. 72 loop consume. The records must agree with the review, and a window with no intervention closes with a dated nil record. Produces __intervention_record__, from which __intervention_record_id__ and __intervention_type__ are extracted.

nodes.name: emit_oversight_evidence

parameters.pythonCode:
from content.playbooks.ai_human_oversight.primitives.evidence import compose_oversight_evidence
__oversight_evidence__ = compose_oversight_evidence(roster=__oversight_roster__, briefing=__briefing_record__, disposition=__review_disposition__, intervention=__intervention_record__, workflow_id=__workflow_id__, execution_id=__execution_id__, captured_at=__captured_at__)

nodes.notes: Compose the dated cycle-evidence artifact joining the roster, the briefings, the review dispositions and the interventions for __deployment_id__ over __oversight_cycle__. This is what an auditor or market-surveillance authority reads to establish that oversight was exercised, not merely assigned: a named overseer who never reviewed anything satisfies Art. 26(2) on paper and Art. 14 not at all, so oversight counts as exercised only with an effective roster, everyone briefed, and every flagged decision dispositioned. The evidence store is an operator-owned surface. Produces __oversight_evidence__, from which __oversight_evidence_id__ is extracted.

nodes.name: ai_human_oversight_end
nodes.notes: Terminal state. The cycle closes on the dated evidence artifact; the next oversight window re-enters at the start step.

## EU AI Act Article 14 human-oversight operating loop
`playbook.ai_human_oversight@v1` · content v1.0.0 · maturity: stable · compiled from a CACAO 2.0 playbook by SecOps-NG

SKELETON — CACAO v2 scaffold for the deployer-side EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) Article 14 human-oversight loop: the cycle an oversight function actually runs once oversight of a high-risk AI system has been assigned. Article 14 straddles the provider/deployer line — Art. 14(1) and 14(3)(a) require the provider to design the system so it can be effectively overseen and to build in what it can, while Art. 14(3)(b) and 14(4) reach the deployer, who implements the meas…

**Controls:** 2 control reference(s) in the canonical source, mapped under `content/mappings/`.

**Before you run it**
- Inputs the trigger expects from you: `__deployment_id__`, `__oversight_cycle__`, `__roster_entries__`, `__roster_resolved_at__`, `__instructions_ref__`, `__briefings__`, `__briefing_recorded_at__`, `__flagged_decisions__`, `__reviews__`, `__biometric_record__`, `__reviewed_at__`, `__interventions__`, `__intervention_recorded_at__`, `__workflow_id__`, `__execution_id__`, `__captured_at__`
- Code nodes name the deterministic primitive each step runs; bind them to where your primitives execute, or replace the body:
  - establish_oversight_roster → `content.playbooks.ai_human_oversight.primitives.roster.resolve_oversight_roster`
  - brief_oversight_personnel → `content.playbooks.ai_human_oversight.primitives.briefing.compose_briefing_record`
  - review_flagged_decisions → `content.playbooks.ai_human_oversight.primitives.review.review_flagged_decisions`
  - record_intervention → `content.playbooks.ai_human_oversight.primitives.intervention.record_interventions`
  - emit_oversight_evidence → `content.playbooks.ai_human_oversight.primitives.evidence.compose_oversight_evidence`
- This file carries no credentials; connectors and secrets are yours to attach.

**Source** https://github.com/secops-ng/secops-ng-framework/tree/main/content/playbooks/ai_human_oversight
